summary: Validated the new IslandHop in-app wallet + CariPay (MOCK) integration. NEW /app/backend/tests/test_wallet.py = 36/36 PASS. Regression /app/backend/tests/test_islandhop_backend.py + /app/backend/tests/test_payments.py = 48/48 PASS. Total backend: 84/84 (100%). All wallet error cases (4xx semantics) verified: 401 unauth, 400 unknown currency / amount-out-of-range / unlinked-deposit / insufficient-balance / empty-handle / self-send, 404 unknown-recipient / unknown-order, plus webhook idempotency (replay returns duplicate:true, no double-credit), unknown-handle ignored, invalid JSON 400. Balances reconcile exactly across deposit/withdraw/p2p/pay-order. Multi-currency works for all 7 supported currencies (USD, JMD, TTD, BBD, GHS, NGN, ZAR).

minor.issue: On insufficient balance the handler returns 400 via a pre-check (line 4280), which is correct. But the post-debit failure path (CariPay declines / throws) reverses by issuing _credit_wallet — not atomic with the debit. Race window is microscopic given MOCK is synchronous, but document for when MOCK_CARIPAY=false. Recommendation: use a single `findAndModify` with a 'pending' txn status, then settle.

Double-pay race: between the balance check (line 4378) and the orders update (line 4382), two concurrent requests could both pass the check and debit twice. The orders update uses `payment_status: {$ne:'paid'}` guard so the order can only be marked paid once, but the SECOND request would still debit the wallet and create an order_payment txn for an order that subsequently isn't marked paid (well, it IS already paid by the first call; the second call's debit becomes a 'lost' debit since the orders update matches 0 docs but the wallet was already decremented). Recommend doing the orders guard update FIRST (acquire lock) and only debit if matched_count==1.

Webhook accepts any currency string and upper-cases it (line 4414). If a malicious/buggy upstream sends `currency: 'XYZ'`, the code calls _credit_wallet with an unsupported currency and creates a balances.XYZ field via $inc. Recommend validating against SUPPORTED_WALLET_CURRENCIES and returning {ignored:true, reason:'unsupported_currency'} otherwise.

Amount precision: payload.amount is `float` with no rounding. Floats like 10.10 + 0.20 + 0.05 can produce 10.349999... in JS clients. Server should round to 2 decimal places (currencies like USD/JMD are minor-unit=cents). Recommend using `round(amount, 2)` server-side and persisting integer cents internally.

action_items: (MEDIUM) /api/wallet/pay-order — flip order of operations: do the `orders.update_one({id, payment_status:{$ne:'paid'}}, ...)` FIRST and check matched_count==1 BEFORE debiting the wallet. Today, two concurrent pay-order calls on the same order debit the wallet twice but only mark paid once.
(LOW) /api/webhook/caripay — validate `currency` against SUPPORTED_WALLET_CURRENCIES; today an unknown currency string creates a brand-new balances.<CCY> field.
(LOW) Add server-side rounding (round-half-even, 2dp) on amount inputs to /api/wallet/{deposit,withdraw,send,pay-order} to avoid float drift.

(LOW) /api/wallet/withdraw — non-atomic debit/CariPay/refund. Reorder to: insert pending txn → call CariPay → on success debit + mark completed; on failure mark failed. Reduces double-spend risk when MOCK_CARIPAY=false.
critical_code_review_comments: Wallet.balances is Dict[str,float] with $inc — correct atomic primitive; concurrent deposits/withdrawals are safe at the Mongo layer.
_debit_wallet uses `{balances.<CCY>: {$gte: amount}}` filter — proper compare-and-set; prevents over-debiting from a SINGLE process. Good.

P2P send debits sender then credits recipient with no transaction wrapper — if the credit step fails (extremely unlikely with $inc upsert) the sender is debited without recipient credited. Acceptable for MVP but recommend session-level transactions when scaling.
Webhook idempotency keyed on external_transfer_id is correct and verified by test. Good.

verify_webhook_signature short-circuits to True in MOCK mode (caripay_client.py:88-89) — this is documented and intentional; flag in deploy checklist that MOCK_CARIPAY must be flipped to false in prod.
GET /api/wallet auto-creates wallet on first read (line 4170). This is convenient but means GET has a side-effect; consider POST /api/wallet for explicit creation if strict REST semantics are needed.

_record_txn signature uses **fields — silently swallows unknown kwargs at the Pydantic layer (WalletTransaction accepts only declared fields); fine but adding `model_config = ConfigDict(extra='forbid')` would catch typos at dev time.

POST /api/wallet/send recipient lookup uses `email.lower().strip()` but registration stores email AS-PROVIDED. If a user registers with `Foo@Bar.com`, p2p_send with recipient_email='foo@bar.com' returns 404. Recommend normalising email to lowercase on register OR using a case-insensitive collation on the users.email index. (Verified during test run — had to lowercase test emails to make p2p work.)
server.py is now 5028 lines (was 4505 in iteration_3). The wallet module is well-bounded (lines 4124–4443) and a perfect candidate to extract into routers/wallet.py.
Duplicate `class OrderItem(BaseModel)` at server.py lines ~134 and ~619 still present — re-flagged from iteration_3, still untouched.
test_credentials: Fresh users registered per test run with unique lowercase emails (walletA_<ts>_<uid>@test.com etc.) / Test1234!. JWT Bearer auth only.
seed_data_creation: Per run: 2 'wallet' users (walletA, walletB) + 3 disposable users for negative-path tests (nodlink, nowlink, hookuser). Each is registered, optionally linked to a CariPay handle, then deposited/withdrew/sent/received. 1 webhook-target user with a unique handle. 2 throwaway orders for pay-order tests. No persistent fixtures — DB grows monotonically.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Three pytest suites cover the backend now: test_islandhop_backend.py (27 cases, core), test_payments.py (21 cases, Stripe/Connect/payouts), test_wallet.py (36 cases, IslandHop wallet + MOCK CariPay). Total 84 cases @ 100%. All read REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL. CariPay is fully mocked via /app/backend/caripay_client.py — flip MOCK_CARIPAY=false in /app/backend/.env to switch to real HTTP (will require filling in _real_deposit/_real_withdrawal once CariPay's API is live). Webhook in MOCK mode skips HMAC verification (verify_webhook_signature returns True). Action items focus on (a) pay-order race window — reorder ops so order-lock happens BEFORE wallet debit, and (b) email case-insensitivity bug in users lookup (affects /api/wallet/send when recipient registered with mixed-case email).
rca of the issue: No active bugs. Initial test-run failures were test-script issues only: (1) OrderCreate model requires `customer_id` in the payload even though the server overrides it — fixed by adding `customer_id: 'will_be_overridden'` to match the test_payments.py pattern; (2) registration emails containing uppercase characters (walletA…) did not match the p2p_send lookup which normalises to lowercase — fixed by lowercasing emails at registration in the test. Both fixes are in /app/backend/tests/test_wallet.py. No server-side code was modified.
